candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity: use therapeutic communication; assess and support client coping and psychosocial responses to health alterations and changes in body image/self-concept.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — altered body image, intimacy concerns, therapeutic communication, and coping after ostomy
candidate.educational_objective: Address ostomy-related body-image and intimacy concerns with open-ended, nonjudgmental communication and offer individualized ostomy and psychosocial support resources when desired.

options.A: It is best to avoid discussing body image until you feel ready to bring it up again.
options.B: Tell me what worries you most about how the ostomy may affect your relationship. We can also discuss ostomy-nurse or support resources if you want them.
options.C: Most people adjust quickly once they learn how to manage the pouch.
options.D: For now, focus on learning pouch care; intimacy concerns can be addressed after physical recovery is complete.

candidate.rationale: NCBI Nursing Skills notes that an ostomy can affect self-esteem, body image, quality of life, and intimacy and that nurses can promote healthy coping through appropriate referrals to a wound/ostomy specialist, social worker, or support groups. Therapeutic communication guidance emphasizes client-centered, nonjudgmental listening and open-ended questions. B acknowledges the concern, invites the client to describe its personal meaning, and offers resources without forcing them. A and D avoid an important psychosocial concern, while C gives premature reassurance and assumes a predictable adjustment course.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Ostomy-related body-image and intimacy concerns are legitimate nursing assessment/support needs; therapeutic nursing care invites expression and may include referral to ostomy and psychosocial resources.
